checks.source_as_cited: Dean & Ghemawat 2004 MapReduce OSDI; Armstrong 2003 KTH thesis
checks.note: Both exist; citations right. Evidence: secondary lecture notes/summaries of MapReduce, and a search that returned only secondary descriptions of the thesis. MapReduce's non-deterministic semantics is per reduce task: each reduce output equals some sequential execution, but different reduce tasks may correspond to different executions. The claimed 'one committed attempt per task, never a mix' across the whole job is stronger than the paper's guarantee; the synthesis must itself consume one committed attempt per field. The thesis covers supervisors and and/or restart strategies; I could not confirm its treatment of restart intensity (it is clearly in OTP documentation, not seen here).
checks.correction: MapReduce guarantees per-reduce-task consistency only; different reduce tasks may reflect different executions of the same map task. Restart intensity and escalation are firmly documented in OTP; check the thesis text before citing it for this.

checks.note: Evidence: secondary summaries of the paper. A sequencer is an opaque string with lock name, mode and generation number. The server checks validity with Chubby or against its recently observed sequencers, and does not simply compare increasing numbers. For servers that cannot check, Chubby offers lock-delay, which does not fully prevent split-brain.
checks.correction: Sequencer validity is checked against Chubby or the server's own cache, not by a plain 'reject older number' rule; the monotonic fencing-token formulation is a later, cleaner statement of the idea.

checks.note: From knowledge, not fetched. The suspicion level is phi = -log10 of the probability that a heartbeat arrives later than now, with a distribution fitted to a sliding window (normal approximation). The false-suspicion probability is only as good as the fit.
checks.correction: Add that the fitted distribution is an approximation, so the probability is only as accurate as that fit.

result.overall: All 24 citations name real works with correct authors, years and venues. This rests on web searches for only three items (MapReduce semantics, Chubby sequencers, Armstrong's restart rule) and my recall of the standard records for the rest, which I did not fetch. Three claims are overstated. First, MapReduce's non-deterministic guarantee is per reduce task, so it does not give a job-wide single-execution guarantee. Second, Chubby sequencers are validated against Chubby or the server's cache, not by a plain monotonic-number check. Third, the thesis was not confirmed to state restart intensity; OTP documentation does. Minor softening is also needed for Helland 2012 and phi accrual.
